terminal_qualifier: high-impact hypotheses KILLED; a low-impact, conditional fee-binding behavior was runtime-confirmed and recorded as an observation (not promoted, no severity assigned)
question: Can a permissionless caller of claim spoof minter / claim without a valid entitlement, over-claim past the per-art guards, or exploit the fee-binding gap (excess stuck / underpay subsidized by standing balance) to bypass the fee or drain held funds?
answer: High-impact: No. The phiSignerAddress signature entitlement cannot be forged (no minter spoof / unauthorized mint) and the maxSupply/time/quantity caps are enforced. Fee-binding: confirmed real but bounded/conditional — overpayment to the claim wrapper is stuck (no refund), and underpayment succeeds only when the factory already holds standing balance (itself from a prior overpayer) AND the caller has a valid signer entitlement; the mintFee still flows to the protocol/art. Not an unconditional theft or unauthorized mint.
